help.msg1: 🤖 CazaSpamBot — how it works I'm an anti-spam bot that protects every group where I'm an admin. A ban in one = a ban in all. 🛡️ Protection layers (in order) 1. When someone new joins • If I already banned them in any of your groups → re-ban (synchronized bans). • I check their profile (via the secondary account): name, photo, bio, age. • If the profile is clearly spam (name in another alphabet, bio with porn/promo links, photos all uploaded at once = stolen identity) → direct ban, no warning. • If they appear on global anti-spam lists (CAS, lols.bot) → ban. • If it's a bot added to the group → I kick it and notify you. • If the profile is very legit (photo + old account + normal name) → walks straight in, no verification. • Everyone else → welcome message with a SOY HUMANO (I'M HUMAN) button (muted until they tap it). Suspicious: kick after 30 min. Normal: reminder after 3h. 2. On every message I detect: text in another alphabet, mentions/links to other groups, URL shorteners, deep-links, commercial ads (salaries, offers), channel forwards as the first message, messages with buttons (typical of spam bots), message flooding (antiflood), and patterns I learned from your /spam calls. 3. Special cases I already cover • Bots posting spam (porn buttons) → ban. • Accounts dormant >1 year that reappear citing a bot → ban (hijacked/sold account). • Messages posted via inline bots → I delete + notify you. ⚖️ Trust levels (anti-false-positive) Every user has a trust level from 1 to 10 (10 = trusted veteran, 1 = newcomer). I compute it like this: • Goes up with: messages written in the group, account age in the group, and my having seen them join (clean track record). • Goes down with: active warnings. And if you whitelist them, they jump straight to 10. I act differently depending on the level: • Level 7-10 (high trust) → I almost never act on them. • Level 4-6 (medium) + something suspicious → I ask you privately with ✅Legit / ❌Spam buttons, and I learn from your answer. • Level 1-3 (new/no history) → normal treatment by the rules. On every suspicious message you'll also see a spam level 1-10 (10 = blatantly spam). • My philosophy: better to let a spam slip than to ban a legit user. 🔕 Messages in the group Automatic bans are silent (they don't clutter the chat). Only your manual bans post a little witty message, which auto-deletes after 3h. 👇 I'll send you the command list in the next message.
help.note: 🔒 You're an admin of one of the groups but not the main bot admin. You can see all the information (read-only). The commands that modify things (ban/setwelcome/warn/etc.) can only be run by the bot admin.
help.msg2: 🛠️ Bot commands — reference 📊 View information /start — bot status and quick stats /stats — metrics (in DM it asks which group) /chats — list of groups where the bot operates /recent — last 10 actions. Example: /recent 30 to see the last 30 /comandos — this same guide /alertas — enable or silence informational alerts (deletions, other admins' bans...) 🔧 Moderation (reply to the message or use @user) /ban @user reason — bans across all your groups at once /unban @user — removes the ban /whitelist @user — marks as immune in the current chat /notspam 42 — reverts a false positive (the number is the id shown in /recent) ⚠️ Warns (progressive warnings: default 3 = ban) /warn @user reason or reply to the message /warns (reply to the user) — see their active warnings /rmwarn (reply) — removes the last warning /resetwarns (reply) — clears all warnings /warnlimit 3 — change the limit (no number just shows it) /warnaction ban — what to do at the limit: ban, kick or mute 📚 Train the classifier (reply to a message) /spam — bans the author (in all groups) + reports the message + adds it to the classifier. /legal — marks the message as LEGITIMATE (anti-false-positive, only learns). The bot deletes your command from the group and confirms by DM. /samples — how many samples there are. Example: /samples spam 30 lists 30 spam /forget 5 — deletes sample number 5 (id shown in /samples) /scan — would this be caught? Reply to a message (forwarded to your DM works) and I'll tell you which rules would fire and what structure it has (text, contact, buttons, forward) 🌹 Welcome, rules and services /config — visual panel with buttons: verification, alerts, timings, welcome, rules and cleanup, all at a glance. (aliases /ajustes /panel) /sync on|off — sync settings across ALL groups (ON by default): every change applies to all at once and /config doesn't ask which group. OFF = each group separately. /limpieza — keep groups clean: hide the bot's commands when typing «/» in groups and auto-delete command messages written in the chat (both ON by default). /idioma es|en — bot language (detected from the system by default; Spanish otherwise). The welcome (👋) is independent of verification: you can greet without verifying. /welcome — view the current group's welcome message /setwelcome text — change the welcome (accepts Rose syntax with buttons) /resetwelcome — back to the default welcome /rules — view rules | /setrules text — change them /cleanservice on / off — auto-delete 'X joined the group' messages /verificacion — human verification + welcome. Default: OFF (clean group) + review ON (private suspicious alerts). With no args = view status and options: · on|off (disables verification AND welcome) · avisos on|off (reminder) · accion kick|mute (on failed verification: kick or stay muted) · tiempos N N N · revisar on|off (without verifying in the group: private suspicious alert with buttons) /testwelcome — welcome preview (shows it to you as if you were new) 🔘 Welcome buttons /welcomebuttons — lists the configured buttons /setwelcomebutton Text | https://url — adds a button /setwelcomebutton Text | https://url same — button on the same row /rmwelcomebutton 3 — removes button id 3 (shown in /welcomebuttons) /clearwelcomebuttons — removes all 🏆 Weekly activity top /top — shows the top 5 of the last 7 days (in DM it asks which group) /topweekly on / off — enable or disable the automatic announcement (Sunday 20:00) Filters: text ≥10 chars or messages with media (photo/video/sticker/audio), no repeated greetings, 10s cooldown. 🫡 Greeters (reactions to greetings) /listgreeters — users marked as friendly /setgreeter @user 🫡 🤝 — adds a greeter with reactions (e.g.) /rmgreeter @user — removes it 👥 Reports with @admin (used by group members) Any user replies to a message with @admin; the bot confirms it. If you act (warn/ban/delete), the bot also deletes the original report and posts a thank-you to the reporter. No warnings for whoever reports. ⚙️ Operation mode /shadow on — only logs, doesn't act (test mode) /shadow off — ACTIVE mode (real ban/kick/delete) The change is immediate but doesn't persist across restarts; to make it permanent edit MODE in the server's .env. ℹ️ Useful tips · The id numbers (of sample, action, button, etc.) always appear in the matching list: /recent, /samples, /welcomebuttons... · The numeric user_ids come from the notifications you get in your DM, or via @userinfobot. · In the bot's DM, the query commands (/stats /welcome /rules) show buttons to pick a group if you're in several.
